why: The answer has every step of the copy in the right order: a new array of the same length, then a loop that copies each element by index. But it uses data2.length() twice, and length() is a String method. For an array, length is a field, so this code does not compile. That makes it a multistructural answer with an error, not correct new code at L4.

concepts.quote: int[] copy = new int[data2.length()]; for (int i = 0; i < data2.length(); i++) copy[i] = data2[i];
concepts.why: The plan is right (new array first, then copy element by element), but data2.length() does not compile on an array.
It creates a new int array sized from data2, but the length is written as a method call instead of the field data2.length.

concepts.quote: for (int i = 0; i < data2.length(); i++) copy[i] = data2[i];
concepts.why: The header correctly visits every index from 0 to n-1, but the bound data2.length() is not valid for an array.
It only declares an int index variable and does nothing else with int arithmetic.
